Milling Cutter, Saws, Gear Cutting Tools and Broaches Sectional Committee, PE 11 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Milling Cutter, Saws, Gear Cutting Tools and Broaches Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. 

ISO 6986 : 1983 'Side and face milling ( slotting ) cutters with indexable inserts — Dimensions' 
is the base from which basic dimensions are derived. It has been found necessary to specify 
number of teeth and a separate standard for half side and face cutters using indexable inserts. 
It is a common practice in user industries to build up side and face cutter gangs. 

Double key ways on side and face milling cutters with diameters 100 mm and above, permit 
the cutters to be displaced by half the pitch in relation to each other when used in gangs. 
Such a measure evens the load variation and consequently reduces torsional vibrations caused 
by intermittent machining. 

In the formulation of this standard, not only industry practice and needs are incorporated but 
following standards issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ) 
conti'ibute to the basis: 

Milling cutters — Recommended range of outside diameter 

Indexable hard metal ( carbide ) inserts with wiper edges, without fixing 

hole — Dimensions 

Side and face milling (slotting) cutters with indexable inserts — Dimensions

IS 13244 : 1991 



Indian Standard 



HALF SIDE AND FACE CUTTERS WITH 
INDEXABLE INSERTS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and 
general requirements of half side and face 
milling cutters with indexable inserts having 
cutting edges on periphery and on one side of 
the cutter. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjucts to this standard : 



Title 

Application of carbides for 
machining, ranges of appli- 
cation and colour code 

Dimensions for interchange- 
ability of milling cutters and 
milling arbors with key-drive 

Methods for sampling small 
tools 

Dimensions for indexable 
( throwaway ) carbide inserts 
for milling cutters : Part 2 
Triangular inserts 

3 DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions shall be as given in Table 1. 

4 MATERIAL OF CUTTER BODY 

Cutter body shall be made of alloy steel having 
tensile strength not less than 925 MPa. 



IS No, 
2428 : 1964 

6285 : 1971 

7778 : 1975 

11523 (Part 2) 
1986 



5 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 While the shape and dimension of the 
inserts will be as per IS 11523 ( Part 2 ) : 1986 
the method of mounting and pitch, etc will be 
left to the choice of manufacturer. This also 
includes angle and position of key ways. 

5.2 The cutter will be supplied duly mounted 
with a set of inserts and spares. 



5.3 The dimensions of key 
according to IS 6285 : 1971. 

6 SAMPLING 



ways shall be 



The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall 
be in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

7 DESIGNATION 

Aright hand half side and face milling cutter 
having diameter Z)=100 mm, width L— 26 mm 
and fitted with carbide inserts of range of 
application P 30 according to IS 2428 : 1964 
shall be designated as: 

Half Side and Face milling cutter IS 13244- 
100x26 — P 30. 

8 MARKING 

Each half side and face cutter shall be marked 
with size and manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bareau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Acty 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if 
any, are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in 
possession of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard maybe 
sent to BIS giving the following reference;
